name: Net royalty per copy (what the creator keeps from one sale)
description: The money left for the IP (intellectual property) owner after the store, the printer and the platform are paid. The main measure in this story.
formula_or_numbers: Net royalty = list price - store's cut - printing cost - platform fee
sources: Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes; B&N Press Help Center: Getting paid; Chapter: Lulu pricing (Sep 2026); PublishDrive Help: pricing plans

name: Net margin % (share of the list price the creator keeps)
description: Lets you compare formats and prices on one scale.
formula_or_numbers: Net margin % = net royalty / list price
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)

name: Channel share (store's cut) (also called the take rate)
description: The part of the price the store or wholesaler keeps. It is the biggest cost on almost every route.
formula_or_numbers: Store's cut = list price x (1 - royalty rate), or list price x wholesale discount
worked_or_calculation: KDP pays a 60% print royalty, so the store keeps $16.99 x 40% = $6.80. IngramSpark's 55% wholesale discount: $16.99 x 55% = $9.34.
sources: Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes

name: Cost variance vs KDP (gap to the Amazon KDP (Kindle Direct Publishing) baseline, split by cause)
description: Shows how much more or less each route keeps than KDP, and why.
formula_or_numbers: Variance = route's net - KDP net = store-cut driver + printing driver + fee driver (each driver = KDP's cost - the route's cost)
worked_or_calculation: IngramSpark: store cut -$2.55 + printing -$0.60 + fee -$0.32 = -$3.47 per copy.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes

name: Contribution per unit pair (contribution margin for one print sale plus one ebook sale)
description: What one reader buying both formats adds toward paying back launch costs.
formula_or_numbers: Contribution per pair = print net royalty + ebook net royalty
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)

name: Breakeven point (unit pairs) (sales needed to earn back year-1 fixed costs)
description: How many print-plus-ebook sales it takes before the work is profitable. Lower is better.
formula_or_numbers: Breakeven = Year-1 fixed costs / contribution per pair, rounded up. Fixed costs = platform setup + $85 copyright registration + $1,500 launch budget + 12 x monthly fee
worked_or_calculation: KDP: $1,585 / $10.08 = 157.3, rounded up to 158. IngramSpark: $1,710 / $6.30 = 271.6, rounded up to 272.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); Hypebot on the 2026 USCO fee schedule; ScribeCount: How to publish on IngramSpark

name: Margin of safety (cushion between planned sales and breakeven)
description: How far sales could fall before you stop covering costs.
formula_or_numbers: Margin of safety = (planned sales - breakeven) / planned sales
worked_or_calculation: KDP at 600 planned pairs: (600 - 158) / 600 = 73.7%.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)

name: Switch point (crossover) (monthly sales where a flat fee beats a per-sale fee)
description: Below it, pay-per-sale routes cost less; above it, a subscription costs less.
formula_or_numbers: Switch point = monthly subscription / extra money kept per pair on the subscription route
worked_or_calculation: PublishDrive vs IngramSpark: $13.99 / ($7.14 - $6.30) = 16.6 sales of each format a month. Ebook only vs Draft2Digital: 40.1 a month.
sources: PublishDrive Help: pricing plans; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes; PublishDrive vs Draft2Digital (Apr 2026)

name: Year-1 net (scenarios) (money kept in the first year at a given sales level)
description: Tests whether the ranking holds if sales are slow (10 a month), normal (50) or great (250).
formula_or_numbers: Year-1 net = 12 x (monthly sales x contribution per pair - monthly fee) - platform setup - $85 copyright registration (launch budget excluded)
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)

name: DSO (days sales outstanding)
description: The average number of days between a sale and the cash arriving. Longer waits need more cash on hand.
formula_or_numbers: Days to cash = payment terms in days after month end + about 15 days (the average sale happens mid-month)
worked_or_calculation: B&N Press pays about 30 days after month end: 30 + 15 = 45 days. IngramSpark pays about 90 days after month end: 90 + 15 = 105 days.
sources: B&N Press Help Center: Getting paid; IngramSpark Agreement (Lightning Source); The Book Designer: B&N Press review; Books.by: Draft2Digital comparison

name: Working capital gap (money earned but not yet received)
description: The cash you are owed at a point in time because stores pay late.
formula_or_numbers: Gap = cumulative royalties earned - cumulative cash received
worked_or_calculation: Month 12 of the illustrative launch: $8,361 earned - $7,413 received = $948.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); Written Word Media 2025 Indie Author Survey

name: KENP rate (Kindle Edition Normalized Pages payout rate)
description: What Kindle Unlimited pays per page read, set monthly from a shared pot. Shown per 1,000 pages.
formula_or_numbers: Pay per 1,000 pages = monthly per-page rate x 1,000; average = mean of 12 months; range = highest - lowest
worked_or_calculation: Average $4.55; range $5.01 - $4.19 = $0.82 (20% from low to high).
sources: Profitable.app KENP rate tracker

name: Breakeven lift (extra sales a cheaper option needs just to tie)
description: The bar an A/B test (a test of version A against version B) must clear before switching to a lower price.
formula_or_numbers: Breakeven lift = net per copy of A / net per copy of B - 1
sources: Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)

name: Sample size per group (shoppers each version needs for a trustworthy A/B result)
description: Too few shoppers and a difference may be luck.
formula_or_numbers: Two-proportion z-test at 95% confidence (z = 1.96) and 80% power (z = 0.84) for the breakeven lift
worked_or_calculation: Print price test at a 2% baseline conversion rate and a 21.4% lift: 18,467 shoppers per group. Ebook test at 3%: 7,814.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)

name: 2. Market context
formula_or_numbers: 3.53M self-published ISBNs (International Standard Book Numbers) in 2025, +38.7%; total 4.17M, +32.5%
worked_or_calculation: Growth = 2025 count / 2024 count - 1 = 3,529,980 / 2,545,885 - 1 = 38.7%. Print share of revenue = (hardback $8.2B + paperback $8.0B) / $33.4B = 49%.
sources: Bowker via Publishers Weekly, Mar 2026; Circana BookScan via Publishers Weekly; AAP StatShot Annual Report 2025

name: 5. Gross-to-net
formula_or_numbers: KDP keeps $6.79; IngramSpark $3.33 on a $16.99 paperback
worked_or_calculation: KDP printing = $1.00 + 200 pages x $0.012 = $3.40. IngramSpark fee = 1.875% market access fee x $16.99 = $0.32. Print costs for IngramSpark ($4.00), B&N Press ($3.50) and Lulu ($5.00) are planning estimates.
sources: Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes; B&N Press Help Center: Getting paid; Chapter: Lulu pricing (Sep 2026); PublishDrive Help: pricing plans

name: 6. Cost variance
formula_or_numbers: IngramSpark keeps $3.47 less per copy than KDP; $2.55 of it is the store's cut
worked_or_calculation: Store-cut driver = KDP $6.80 - IngramSpark $9.34 = -$2.55; printing = $3.40 - $4.00 = -$0.60; fee = $0.00 - $0.32 = -$0.32. The three add up to -$3.47.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes

name: 7. Ebooks
formula_or_numbers: Direct uploads keep $3.49; KDP $3.28; Draft2Digital $3.14; IngramSpark $2.97
sources: ScribeCount platform comparison; Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; PublishDrive vs Draft2Digital (Apr 2026); IngramSpark Agreement (Lightning Source)

name: 8. Breakeven
formula_or_numbers: KDP 158 pairs; IngramSpark 272; slowest 511
worked_or_calculation: Year-1 fixed costs = platform setup (ISBN, or International Standard Book Number, $125 where you buy your own) + $85 copyright registration + $1,500 illustrative launch budget + subscription. KDP: $1,585 / $10.08 per pair, rounded up = 158.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); Hypebot on the 2026 USCO fee schedule; ScribeCount: How to publish on IngramSpark; PublishDrive Help: pricing plans

name: 9. Scenarios
formula_or_numbers: KDP Year-1 net $1,124 / $5,961 / $30,146 at 10 / 50 / 250 sales a month; switch point 16.6
worked_or_calculation: 12 x (monthly sales x contribution per pair - monthly fee) - platform setup - $85 copyright. Switch point = $13.99 PublishDrive fee / ($7.14 - $6.30) = 16.6.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); PublishDrive Help: pricing plans

name: 11. Cash timing
formula_or_numbers: $948 owed at month 12; 45 to 105 days to cash
worked_or_calculation: Illustrative launch: 120 sales of each format in month 1, falling 8% a month to 40; 65% on Amazon, 35% elsewhere. KDP and Draft2Digital pay 2 months later, IngramSpark 3. Days to cash = payment terms + about 15 days.
sources: Model in this repository (analysis/model.py); Written Word Media 2025 Indie Author Survey; B&N Press Help Center: Getting paid; IngramSpark Agreement (Lightning Source)

name: 12. Kindle Unlimited
formula_or_numbers: $4.19 to $5.01 per 1,000 pages; average $4.55
worked_or_calculation: Author-reported monthly KENP (Kindle Edition Normalized Pages) rates from May 2025 to April 2026, multiplied by 1,000. Average = sum of 12 months / 12.
sources: Profitable.app KENP rate tracker

name: 13. A/B test
formula_or_numbers: Price cuts need 21% to 27% more sales; store terms 77%
worked_or_calculation: Ebook: KDP net at $4.99 = $3.28, at $3.99 = $2.58, lift = 27.1%. Store terms: IngramSpark net at a 40% non-returnable discount ($5.88) / at 55% returnable ($3.33) - 1 = 76.6%.
sources: Profitable.app KDP royalty calculator; IngramSpark Help Center: 2026 pricing changes; Model in this repository (analysis/model.py)
